Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Changing Dockyard

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Edit content/world.tscn and its .tres geometry/joint resources in Godot for authoritative collision content. The ordinary preparation/build runs the shared bake. Runtime code retains detached values/catalogs/checkpoints and frees the authoring tree; do not query scene nodes from a simulation step.

The current profile is 19 bodies/shapes, eight deduplicated geometries and one hinge. Cosmetic detail belongs in view.gd/feedback.gd, not new physics bodies. Simulation, inputs and authored rules live in modules/dockyard/{model,round,controller}.odin. Changes there alter the rules/cohort and need affected complete-state/game checks.

Presentation consumes copied body frames and a bounded FIFO of confirmed Cue_Route changes. feedback.gd remembers the consumed sequence, so repeated getter calls, late joins and old snapshots cannot replay earlier sounds or bursts. A FIFO gap is counted as unavailable; it does not fabricate an event. The four voices and four 16-instance burst pools are bounded. Keep effects out of the solver and honor reduced-motion/audio settings.

Generate the original WAVs with python3 tests/replay_dockyard/presentation/make_audio.py and retain their hashes. See audio provenance. All primitive meshes, colors and cosmetic animation in this example are authored in repository code; no external art pack is required.

Use F2 for local sound/camera/effects settings, Escape for the crew menu and F3 for actual-data diagnostics. Use the presentation checks for rendered/audio observations, lifecycle checks for network/ownership behavior and the final qualification card for hardware budgets. An automated controller or screenshot cannot supply human co-op feedback.
